o1.biggest_strength: It builds the whole launch around the strongest signals: on-feet worker creators, problem-first hooks, Spark Ads from day 1, and a $38 90-day break-even target checked against Shopify rather than TikTok ROAS.
o1.biggest_mistake: The only notable wobble is the broad targeting note of “no age floor,” which I’d want cleaned up to match platform rules and our adult buyer focus.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the targeting language, assign exact Monday owners by role, and make the reserve release mechanics a little simpler to operate.

o2.biggest_strength: It gets the main economics right, avoids mission-first and discount-first launches, and gives a clear setup, creative, budget, and Day 30 scorecard.
o2.biggest_mistake: Its scale rules and Day 30 pass bar are a bit too strict and inconsistent with the stated $38 target, and “native sound” could create rights issues for paid TikTok ads.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Align all kill, scale, and Day 30 rules to the $38/$57 economics, use commercial-safe audio language, and put the nurse/server Spark Ads more clearly at the center of day-one spend.

reason: Output 1 feels more like a media buyer acting directly on our data and constraints, especially the worker-creator signal, the problem-first hooks, the Shopify-based measurement, and the 90-day break-even logic. Output 2 is solid and usable, but its scaling thresholds and scorecard would make it harder to decide fairly whether TikTok has earned more budget.
